data.component: unbound rebinding protection (private-address) applied to forwarded .lan answers
data.cause: gw.lan's unbound forwards .lan to dns1 but its DNS-rebinding protection (private-address: 10.0.0.0/8) discards the legitimate private answer 10.20.0.50 for nas.lan, so whenever dns1's aggressive ratelimiter (20 q/s per /24, log entries at 02:14, 09:41, 13:02 show bursts of dropped queries) temporarily drops queries, the client's fallback to gw.lan returns an empty NOERROR instead of the address, producing intermittent ENOTFOUND for local names only; internet names still resolve because their public answers aren't filtered and the fallback path works.
evidence: dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan on mon.lan returns 'nas.lan. 10 IN A 10.20.0.50' — dns1 answers correctly most of the time
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan on mon.lan returns status NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 — gw.lan replies with no address for the same name
/etc/resolv.conf on mon.lan lists nameserver 10.20.0.3 then 10.20.0.1, so every rate-limited lookup falls through to gw.lan

journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan shows repeated 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping N queries' events (Mar 03 02:14, 09:41, 13:02) followed by 'back under limit' within seconds — matches alerts a few times a day that clear within a minute or two
/opt/primary-dns/config.yaml sets ratelimit: 20 and rewrites *.lan / nas.lan to 10.20.0.50 with a 10-second TTL, so bursts hit the limiter and caching can't mask it
/var/unbound/unbound.conf on gw.lan contains 'private-address: 10.0.0.0/8' alongside 'forward-zone: name "lan." forward-addr: 10.20.0.3', which explains the empty NOERROR answer for nas.lan from gw
data.recommendation: Fix the backup path on gw.lan's unbound so it can serve local names: exempt the forwarded .lan zone from the private-address rebinding filter (e.g., tag the lan forward-zone/view so 10.20.0.0/8 answers are allowed for it, or move private-address handling into a view that permits the authoritative .lan data), while keeping the filter for the public "." zone. Optionally also raise dns1's ratelimit above the observed burst rate so the primary rarely drops client queries; do not remove the rebinding protection for internet names.
